title: CRISPRi-mediated silencing of retrotransposons in human pluripotent stem cells
author: Adami, Garza, et al.
materials: NucleoSpin PCR Cleanup and Gel Extraction

steps.title: Map reads with STAR
steps.instruction: Run STAR aligner version 2.7.8a on the bulk RNA‑seq FASTQ files using the latest genome index and the GENCODE annotation GTF supplied via the --sjdbGTFfile option. Restrict alignments to uniquely mapped reads with --outFilterMultimapNmax 1 and limit mismatches to 3 % of the read length with --outFilterMismatchNoverLmax 0.03.

substeps.instruction: Execute STAR with –-sjdbGTFfile pointing to the GENCODE GTF file.
Add –-outFilterMultimapNmax 1 to keep only single‑locus mappings.
Add –-outFilterMismatchNoverLmax 0.03 to enforce a 0.03 mismatch‑to‑length ratio.

steps.title: Generate strand‑specific bigwig files (optional)
steps.instruction: From the STAR‑generated BAM/SAM files, create strand‑specific bigwig tracks using bamCoverage from deeptools version 2.4.5, then feed those bigwigs into computeMatrix and plotHeatmap (deeptools) to visualise heatmaps for the L1 subfamilies of interest.

substeps.instruction: Run bamCoverage (deeptools v2.4.5) on the alignment file to produce separate forward‑ and reverse‑strand bigwig files.
Provide the bigwig files to computeMatrix to compute the matrix of signal over L1 loci.
Use plotHeatmap to generate heatmaps displaying L1 subfamily expression.

steps.title: Create strand‑specific count matrices
steps.instruction: Separate the alignment file by strand using samtools view (version 1.16.1) based on SAM flags, then generate count matrices for evolutionarily young L1 elements from each strand‑specific file.

substeps.instruction: Run samtools view –f 0x10 (or appropriate flag) to extract reverse‑strand reads and samtools view –F 0x10 for forward‑strand reads.
Count reads overlapping young L1 annotations in each strand‑specific BAM to build count matrices.

steps.title: Define upstream custom GTF entries
steps.instruction: Add custom GTF entries representing regions 500 bp upstream of each L1 transcription‑start site, oriented opposite to the L1 direction, to capture L1‑ORF0‑derived transcription.

steps.title: Select top gRNAs for validation
steps.instruction: Analyze the bulk RNA‑seq results to identify gRNAs that most effectively and specifically silence young L1s; choose 1–3 of the best‑performing gRNAs for downstream experiments.

description: Transposable elements (TEs) are repetitive sequences that have colonised the human genome throughout evolution and comprise approximately 50% of the human genome.2,3 Historically viewed as genomic relics, TEs have been severely understudied. Their repetitive nature poses considerable challenges in the investigation of these elements; however, recent advances in sequencing technologies and off-target-minimised CRISPR-based approaches now enable thorough TE investigation at the locus-specific and subfamily levels. Still, downstream on- and off-target analyses of transcriptional manipulations are needed to validate the specificity of these tools and ensure that any observed phenotypic effect in a chosen in vitro model is in fact a consequence of the TE manipulation. The protocol described below provides detailed steps for designing gRNAs to target TE families (multiple copies) using CRISPR inhibition (CRISPRi) and to validate the successful targeting of multiple sequences. Specifically, we present a solid framework to thoroughly assess the specific and efficient silencing of evolutionarily young long interspersed nuclear elements-1 (L1s) (Figure 1) in human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs). Recent studies have shown that L1s are functionally embedded into transcriptional regulatory networks1,4,5 and play a significant role in embryonic development by influencing the chromatin state of their genomic location.6,7 Thus, it is relevant to investigate L1s in their specific genomic context, which can be achieved, for instance, via their transcriptional manipulation using CRISPRi, as described here.Figure 1Long interspersed nuclear elements (LINE-1s)Left: Overview of the structure of a full-length, evolutionarily young L1 elements which include an intact 5′ untranslated region (UTR), three open reading frames (ORFs), and a 3′ UTR. Right: Phylogenetic tree showing the evolutionary age of the younger L1 subfamilies. This protocol can also be used to design gRNAs for CRIS
